# fkr

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/yng-me/fkr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/yng-me/fkr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://github.com/yng-me/fkr/blob/main/LICENSE.md)
<!-- badges: end -->

**fkr** generates realistic-looking, made-up (fake) data for the
Philippines -- names, addresses, phone numbers, ages, job titles, ID-style
numbers, and more -- for building and testing software, writing tutorials,
or teaching, **without using any real person's information.**

Nothing this package produces is looked up from a real database. Every
value -- including anything formatted to look like a government ID number
(SSS, TIN, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, PhilSys) -- is randomly made up on the spot.
It does not belong to any real person, business, or record, and won't work
anywhere official.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("yng-me/fkr")
```

## Quick start

Every function starts with `fkr_`. The first thing you tell it is always
**how many fake values you want**:

```{r example}
library(fkr)

fkr_full_name(3)
fkr_age(3)
fkr_mobile_number(3)
fkr_address(3)
```

Want a whole pretend dataset -- many columns, many rows -- in one go? Use
`fkr()` and list which generator fills each column:

```{r dataset-example}
fkr(5, list(
  first_name = fkr_first_name,
  last_name = fkr_last_name,
  sex = fkr_sex,
  age = fkr_age,
  date_of_birth = fkr_birthday
))
```

`age` and `date_of_birth` automatically agree with each other -- fkr
makes sure a person's birthdate actually matches the age shown for them.

For a friendlier, step-by-step walkthrough (including how to attach extra
settings to a column, or make one column depend on another), see
`vignette("fkr")` after installing.

## What can it generate?

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| People | first/last/full name, sex, civil status, age, birthday |
| Contact details | email, mobile number, landline number |
| Addresses | region, province, city, barangay, street address, ZIP code, full address |
| Government ID-style numbers | SSS, TIN, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, PhilSys (see disclaimer above) |
| Official PH classifications | PSGC geographic codes, PSOC occupations, PSIC industries |
| Business | company name, job title, industry, product, price, business permit number |
| General-purpose helpers | plain numbers, whole numbers, yes/no, "select all that apply", labeled categories, unique IDs, coordinates |
| Whole datasets | `fkr()` -- build a complete fake table in one call |

Every function has its own help page with more detail and examples, e.g.
`?fkr_address`.

## A note on realism

Names, surnames, addresses, and job titles are drawn from real Philippine
reference data where possible (e.g. actual region/province/city names,
and the official PSGC, PSOC, and PSIC classification systems), so the
*shape* of the data is realistic -- but the specific combination assigned
to any one fake record is always random and fictional.
